newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures build gains, end higher.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures build gains, end higher.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures built gains in fairly brisk late trading to close a short trading session higher and near day's peaks.
Currency futures ended two hours early Thursday at 1200 CST/1800 GMT and will stay shut Friday for the long holiday weekend. Normal trading hours will resume Monday, March 31.
Futures began heading higher again as U.S. Treasury bonds and equities expanded losses, with T-bond futures slicing below key support zones in technically oriented activity.
Currency brokers noted signs of fund buying in yen and unwinding of long sterling/short mark spreads late.
"It was ugly," said one floor broker of late trade in yen. "The funds were buying."
Canadian dollar sagged more late, with one Japanese-owned bank seen a featured seller as June futures slipped quickly from $0.7295 to $0.7288.

Earlier, June Swiss francs staged a strong rally, hitting buy stops at $0.6942 and again near $0.6955 on good volume that brokers figured stemmed from short-covering rather than fresh buying, given concerns that U.S. rates are headed higher.
"The dollar should be bid on this," said another broker. "I think we're just seeing mostly short-covering on this."

Yen had risen overnight after U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said the United States remained concerned about the "dangerous possibility" that Japan's current account surplus would expand substantially.

Debt and equity index futures began eroding in earnest after stronger than expected February U.S. existing home sales, which jumped 9.0 percent to a 4.26 million unit rate compared to forecasts for a rise to a 4.05 million unit rate.
Fourth-quarter U.S. real gross domestic product and February new home sales are due Friday when futures are shut. New home sales are seen at 811,000 units vs January's 870,000.
GDP is expected to have grown at a 4.0 percent rate with the price index showing a 1.8 percent increase and the implicit deflator gaining 1.4 percent.

Brokers said they doubted players would get too stirred up about missing Friday's figures, and some noted that many European centers will still be out Monday when the March Chicago purchasing managers index and other data are due.

June yen rose $0.000037 to $0.008193, mark up $0.0058 at $0.6008, Swiss franc up $0.0090 to $0.6969, sterling up $0.0024 to $1.6298, Can dollar fell $0.0036 to $0.7288, Aussie dollar off $0.0010 at $0.7829, Mexican peso off $0.000325 at $0.122375.
